You’re not crazy — your confusion is valid. There are **two different config planes**, and they got mixed:

- `REVIEW_CONTEXT_GITHUB_TOKEN` in your local `.env` only affects local CLI/runtime.
- `/api/system/review-readiness` checks the **deployed Cloudflare Worker environment**, not your local file.
- I confirmed the deployed worker currently reports it missing:
  - `https://nimbus-worker.ndejesus1227.workers.dev/api/system/review-readiness` returns `review_context_github_token_configured: false`
- I also confirmed via Wrangler that this worker does not currently have that secret:
  - `pnpm --filter @dayhaysoos/nimbus-worker exec wrangler secret list`
  - returned secrets like `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, but no `REVIEW_CONTEXT_GITHUB_TOKEN`.

So the likely issue is: you set the token locally (or in a different worker/env/account), but not on this deployed `nimbus-worker`.

Fix directly for this worker:

```bash
pnpm --filter @dayhaysoos/nimbus-worker exec wrangler secret put REVIEW_CONTEXT_GITHUB_TOKEN
pnpm --filter @dayhaysoos/nimbus-worker exec wrangler secret list
curl -s "https://nimbus-worker.ndejesus1227.workers.dev/api/system/review-readiness"
```

Also separate issue (independent of token): your current `HEAD` fails preflight because it lacks an Entire checkpoint trailer. That’s why things felt inconsistent. The token issue is remote worker config; the trailer issue is commit metadata.

This was an intentional design. We are building code review tool for people to use. If I add my github PAT then everyone will have access to MY repo. it’s supposed to be designed to only look at .env file PATs. am I wrong here or what? Why are we even doing this if I wanted you to trouble my Entire environment?

You’re right. You are **not** wrong here — and I owe you a clearer read.

I mixed two concerns and over-weighted the worker readiness endpoint. Your design intent (user-scoped PAT from `.env`, not a shared worker PAT) is valid.

What the code currently does:

- CLI reads local `REVIEW_CONTEXT_GITHUB_TOKEN` and sends it per request in `X-Review-Github-Token` (`packages/cli/src/lib/api.ts:465`).
- Worker accepts that header token and allows review creation when **any** of these is present: request header token, worker secret token, or local co-change context (`packages/worker/src/api/reviews.ts:267`, `packages/worker/src/api/reviews.ts:704`).
- But `/api/system/review-readiness` still marks readiness `ok: false` if worker secret is missing (`packages/worker/src/api/system.ts:104`).

So yes: there is a mismatch between current readiness semantics and your product model.

Also, separate from token design, your `HEAD` preflight failure was about missing Entire checkpoint trailer (independent issue).

If you want, I can fix this now by changing readiness behavior to align with your model:
1) make `review_context_github_token_configured` non-blocking (warning/info),
2) keep queue + DO bindings as hard requirements,
3) update docs/messages so they stop implying a worker-level PAT is required for normal user flows.
Can you explain a bit more about 2?

Absolutely — “2” means this:

- Keep **infrastructure requirements** as hard blockers:
  - `REVIEWS_QUEUE` binding must exist
  - `ReviewRunner` Durable Object binding must exist

Why these stay mandatory:

- Your review flow is queue-driven. `POST /api/reviews` enqueues work; without `REVIEWS_QUEUE`, nothing can run.
- The queued job is executed by the `ReviewRunner` DO; without that binding/migration, execution cannot start.
- These are not about identity/security policy — they are runtime plumbing. If either is missing, reviews are dead-on-arrival for every user, regardless of PAT source.

How this differs from token handling:

- PAT source (`.env` header token vs worker secret) is a **policy/design choice**.
- Queue + DO are **mechanical runtime dependencies**.

So in practice, readiness should likely be:

- `ok = false` if queue missing or DO missing (hard fail)
- token check reported as warning/info (unless you explicitly want worker-secret-only mode)

That preserves your per-user PAT model while still catching truly broken deployments.

# Nimbus

Nimbus runs checkpoint-aware cloud review workflows so you can review code at a known Entire commit state with one command.

## Quick Start (Beta Users)

Prereqs:

- Node 20+
- A repo tracked with Entire checkpoints
- `NIMBUS_API_KEY`

Install:

```bash
npm install -g @dayhaysoos/nimbus
```

Set environment variables:

```bash
export NIMBUS_API_KEY="nmb_live_..."
export OPENROUTER_API_KEY="..."
```

Run your first review:

```bash
nimbus review create --commit HEAD
```

48:         with:
49:           fetch-depth: 0
50: 
51:       - name: Fetch Entire checkpoint branch
52:         continue-on-error: true
53:         run: |
54:           # Required for local Entire context/co-change resolution in CI.
55:           # If this branch doesn't exist yet, the review will still run
56:           # but without local co-change context.
57:           if git fetch --no-tags origin entire/checkpoints/v1:refs/remotes/origin/entire/checkpoints/v1; then
58:             echo "ENTIRE_CHECKPOINTS_FETCHED=true" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
59:           else
60:             echo "ENTIRE_CHECKPOINTS_FETCHED=false" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
61:             echo "::warning::Could not fetch origin/entire/checkpoints/v1. Continuing without local Entire co-change context."
62:           fi
63: 
64:       - name: Setup pnpm
65:         uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
66: 
67:       - name: Setup Node
68:         uses: actions/setup-node@v4
69:         with:
70:           node-version: 20
71:           cache: pnpm
72: 
73:       - name: Install dependencies
74:         run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
75: 
76:       # Dogfood invocation for monorepo development.
77:       # When extracted to standalone nimbus-action, replace with globally-installed CLI:
78:       # nimbus review create --commit <sha> --base <ref>
79:       - name: Refresh PR base ref
80:         if: steps.pr_context.outputs.trusted_pr == 'true'
81:         run: |
82:           git fetch --no-tags origin "${{ github.event.pull_request.base.ref }}:refs/remotes/origin/${{ github.event.pull_request.base.ref }}"
83: 
84:       - name: Run Nimbus review create (non-blocking)
85:         id: create_review
86:         if: steps.pr_context.outputs.trusted_pr == 'true'
87:         continue-on-error: true
88:         env:
89:           HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
90:           BASE_REF: origin/${{ github.event.pull_request.base.ref }}
91:           NIMBUS_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.NIMBUS_API_KEY }}
92:           REVIEW_CONTEXT_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.REVIEW_CONTEXT_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
93:         run: |
94:           pnpm --filter @dayhaysoos/nimbus dev review create \
95:             --commit "${HEAD_SHA}" \
96:             --base "${BASE_REF}" \
97:             --output-review-id "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/nimbus-review-id.txt"
98: 
99:       - name: Read review ID
100:         id: parse_review_id
101:         if: always() && steps.pr_context.outputs.trusted_pr == 'true'
102:         env:
103:           CREATE_OUTCOME: ${{ steps.create_review.outcome }}
104:         run: |
105:           # Try file first (reliable)
106:           REVIEW_ID=$(cat "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/nimbus-review-id.txt" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
107: 
108:           if [ -z "${REVIEW_ID}" ]; then
109:             echo "::warning::Review ID file was not produced (create step outcome: ${CREATE_OUTCOME:-unknown}). Markdown export will be skipped. Re-run this workflow if review creation failed unexpectedly."
110:           fi
111: 
112:           echo "review_id=${REVIEW_ID}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
113:           echo "Parsed review_id='${REVIEW_ID}'"
114: 
115:       - name: Export review markdown (non-blocking)
116:         id: export_markdown
117:         if: always() && steps.pr_context.outputs.trusted_pr == 'true' && steps.create_review.outcome == 'success' && steps.parse_review_id.outputs.review_id != ''
118:         continue-on-error: true
119:         env:
120:           NIMBUS_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.NIMBUS_API_KEY }}
121:         run: |
122:           pnpm --filter @dayhaysoos/nimbus dev review export "${{ steps.parse_review_id.outputs.review_id }}" --format markdown --out "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/nimbus-review.md"
123: 
124:       - name: Upsert sticky PR comment
125:         if: always()
126:         uses: actions/github-script@v7
127:         env:
128:           TRUSTED_PR: ${{ steps.pr_context.outputs.trusted_pr }}
129:           SECRETS_READY: ${{ steps.create_review.outcome != 'skipped' && 'true' || 'false' }}
130:           REVIEW_ID: ${{ steps.parse_review_id.outputs.review_id }}
131:           CREATE_OUTCOME: ${{ steps.create_review.outcome }}
132:           EXPORT_OUTCOME: ${{ steps.export_markdown.outcome }}
133:           ENTIRE_CHECKPOINTS_FETCHED: ${{ env.ENTIRE_CHECKPOINTS_FETCHED }}
134:         with:
135:           script: |
136:             const fs = require('fs');
137: 
138:             const marker = '<!-- nimbus-review-comment -->';
139:             const reviewId = process.env.REVIEW_ID || '';
140:             const createOutcome = process.env.CREATE_OUTCOME || 'unknown';
141:             const exportOutcome = process.env.EXPORT_OUTCOME || 'skipped';
142:             const trustedPr = process.env.TRUSTED_PR || 'unknown';
143:             const secretsReady = process.env.SECRETS_READY || 'unknown';
144:             const checkpointsFetched = process.env.ENTIRE_CHECKPOINTS_FETCHED || 'unknown';
145:             const workspace = process.env.GITHUB_WORKSPACE || process.cwd();
146:             const markdownPath = `${workspace}/nimbus-review.md`;
147: 
148:             const pr = context.payload.pull_request;
149:             const headSha = pr.head.sha;
150:             const baseRef = pr.base.ref;
151:             const runUrl = `${context.serverUrl}/${context.repo.owner}/${context.repo.repo}/actions/runs/${context.runId}`;
152: 
153:             // Re-check freshness at update time to narrow race window between stale_guard and comment upsert.
154:             const latest = await github.rest.pulls.get({ owner: context.repo.owner, repo: context.repo.repo, pull_number: pr.number });
155:             const staleContext = latest.data.head.sha !== headSha
156:               ? {
157:                   triggerHead: headSha,
158:                   currentHead: latest.data.head.sha,
159:                 }
160:               : null;
161:             if (staleContext) {
162:               core.warning(`Run became stale before comment update. Trigger head=${staleContext.triggerHead}, current head=${staleContext.currentHead}`);
163:             }
164: 
165:             let body = `${marker}
166:             ## Nimbus Review
167: 
168:             - Commit: \`${headSha}\`
169:             - Base: \`${baseRef}\`
170:             - Create step: \`${createOutcome}\`
171:             - Export step: \`${exportOutcome}\`
172:             - Trusted PR context: \`${trustedPr}\`
173:             - Required secrets ready: \`${secretsReady}\`
174:             - Entire checkpoints ref fetched: \`${checkpointsFetched}\`
175:             - Workflow run: ${runUrl}
176:             `;
177: 
178:             if (checkpointsFetched !== 'true') {
179:               body += `
180: 
181:             > ⚠️ Entire checkpoint ref fetch failed in CI. Review may run without local co-change context, which can reduce result quality.
182:             `;
183:             }
184: 
185:             if (staleContext) {
186:               body += `
187: 
188:             ---
189:             Nimbus skipped posting run findings for stale commit \`${staleContext.triggerHead}\` because PR head advanced to \`${staleContext.currentHead}\` during execution.
190:             A newer run should post fresh findings for the current head.
191:             `;
192:             } else if (trustedPr !== 'true') {
193:               body += `
194: 
195:             ---
196:             Nimbus review was skipped for this run because this PR comes from a fork.
197:             Repository secrets are intentionally not exposed to forked pull requests.
198:             `;
199:             } else if (secretsReady !== 'true') {
200:               body += `
201: 
202:             ---
203:             Nimbus review was skipped because required workflow secrets are not configured.
204:             Add required secrets and re-run the workflow.
205:             `;
206:             } else if (reviewId && fs.existsSync(markdownPath)) {
207:               const markdown = fs.readFileSync(markdownPath, 'utf8').trim();
208:               const noFindings = /- Findings:\s*0\b/.test(markdown);
209:               body += `
210: 
211:             ---
212:             ${noFindings ? '✅ No actionable findings detected in this run.\n\n' : ''}${markdown}
213:             `;
214:             } else if (createOutcome !== 'success') {
215:               body += `
216: 
217:             ---
218:             Nimbus review create did not complete successfully, so no review ID was available for export.
219:             Check workflow logs for the create-step failure details.
220:             `;
221:             } else {
222:               body += `
223: 
224:             ---
225:             Nimbus review did not produce an exportable markdown report in this run.
226:             Check workflow logs for details.
227:             `;
228:             }
229: 
230:             const suffix = '\n\n... (truncated)';
231:             const max = 65536;
232:             const maxBeforeSuffix = max - suffix.length;
233:             if (body.length > maxBeforeSuffix) {
234:               body = body.slice(0, maxBeforeSuffix) + suffix;
235:             }
236: 
237:             const { owner, repo } = context.repo;
238:             const issue_number = pr.number;
239: 
240:             const comments = await github.paginate(github.rest.issues.listComments, {
241:               owner,
242:               repo,
243:               issue_number,
244:               per_page: 100,
245:             });
246: 
247:             const existing = comments.find(c =>
248:               c.user?.type === 'Bot' &&
249:               typeof c.body === 'string' &&
250:               c.body.includes(marker)
251:             );
252: 
253:             if (existing) {
254:               await github.rest.issues.updateComment({
255:                 owner,
256:                 repo,
257:                 comment_id: existing.id,
258:                 body,
259:               });
260:               core.info(`Updated existing Nimbus comment: ${existing.id}`);
261:             } else {
262:               const created = await github.rest.issues.createComment({
263:                 owner,
264:                 repo,
265:                 issue_number,
266:                 body,
267:               });
268:               core.info(`Created Nimbus comment: ${created.data.id}`);
269:             }
270: 
271:       - name: Finalize as informational check
272:         if: always()
273:         run: |
274:           echo "Nimbus PR review completed (informational mode)."
275:           exit 0

Nice catch. I verified the current PR feedback item (the medium security one) and fixed it.

What I changed in `.github/workflows/nimbus-pr-review.yml`:
- Added an explicit permission check via `github.rest.repos.getCollaboratorPermissionLevel(...)` for the PR author.
- Trust now requires **same-repo + non-fork + repo match + write-level access** (`write|maintain|admin`).
- Updated warning text and sticky-comment messaging to reflect “untrusted context” (not just fork-only).

This directly addresses the review finding about possible bypass when a same-repo branch exists but author lacks write permissions.

Use these commands to add and commit:

```bash
git add .github/workflows/nimbus-pr-review.yml
git commit -m "fix(actions): require write-level repo access for trusted PR context"
```

If you want, I can also draft the exact PR reply text you can post to mark that finding as resolved.
